classification.difficultyReason: Find an exclusive region probability, then use an algebraic probability condition to express one parameter in terms of another.

content.prompt:
A car manufacturer is reviewing the performance of its car model $X$.

It is known that at any given six-month service, the probability of model $X$ requiring an oil change is $\frac{17}{20}$, the probability of model $X$ requiring an air filter change is $\frac{3}{20}$, and the probability of model $X$ requiring both is $\frac{1}{20}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: State the probability that at any given six-month service model $X$ will require an air filter change without an oil change.

answer.worked:
Let $A$ be the event that an air filter change is required and $O$ the event that an oil change is required.

$$\begin{align*}P(A\cap O')&=P(A)-P(A\cap O)\\P(A\cap O')&=\frac{3}{20}-\frac{1}{20}\\P(A\cap O')&=\frac{2}{20}\\P(A\cap O')&=\frac{1}{10}\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Two overlapping circles, Oil on the left and Filter on the right, without a universal-set rectangle or shading. Ordinary outlines and labels use house black.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
The car manufacturer is developing a new model. The production goals are that the probability of model $Y$ requiring an oil change at any given six-month service will be $\frac{m}{m+n}$, the probability of model $Y$ requiring an air filter change will be $\frac{n}{m+n}$ and the probability of model $Y$ requiring both will be $\frac{1}{m+n}$, where $m,n\in\mathbb{Z}^{+}$.

Determine $m$ in terms of $n$ if the probability of model $Y$ requiring an air filter change without an oil change at any given six-month service is $0.05$.

answer.worked:
Let $A$ be the event that an air filter change is required and $O$ the event that an oil change is required.

$$\begin{align*}P(A\cap O')&=P(A)-P(A\cap O)\\P(A\cap O')&=\frac{n}{m+n}-\frac{1}{m+n}\\P(A\cap O')&=\frac{n-1}{m+n}\\\frac{n-1}{m+n}&=\frac{1}{20}\\20(n-1)&=m+n\\20n-20&=m+n\\19n-20&=m\\m&=19n-20\end{align*}$$
